title: Bodley: a provisional register of United States executive orders, their working statuses and source-hashed lifecycle claims (version 1)
description:
Version 1 of the data behind The Afterlife of Executive Orders: a register of 14,998 working bibliographic identities for United States executive orders (the project's census, legal cutoff 14 October 2026), with, for each order, what source documents are held, a provisional yes/no status for whether any operative effect survives the cutoff, and, for 1,527 orders, a filed lifecycle claim with the source hashes and character spans it rests on.

Read this first. The number of orders whose whole lifecycle has been certified by an independent human reviewer is 0. Every status, claim and estimate in this release is an AI-produced working hypothesis that has passed the project's own structural and provenance gates (and, for the statuses, an AI review under written owner rulings); none is a legal finding. Each table carries an explicit evidence-tier label. The 4,298 provisional statuses are not a survival rate for executive orders: the other 10,700 orders have no status yet, and the researched orders were not drawn at random.

What is not here. No licensed text and no bulk source bytes (no PDFs, page images or scans). Every source is cited by URL and SHA-256; every quotation in a claim is replaced by its SHA-256 and length, with the character span kept, so a reader who holds the source bytes can re-verify each span. A hash manifest of the project's byte store is included.

Contents: census identity layer; order register; provisional status ledger with decision origin; per-order readiness and text-evidence tier; filed claims (latest per order) with an index and a table of source references; source and byte-store hash manifests; GPO fixity matches; a stratified-sample estimate (n=120, provisional); the frozen codebook v2.0.0; methods documents and code. Prior datasets on executive-order longevity (Thrower; Lowande and Poznansky) are cited and crosswalked, not redistributed.
notes: Human-certified whole-lifecycle count: 0. All statuses and claims are provisional, AI-produced and uncertified. Source texts are cited by URL and SHA-256 and are not redistributed. Built offline from one commit of https://github.com/D3m0sthene5/Executive-Orders by build_release.py; see MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS.
references: Thrower, S. (2016). Replication Data for: To Revoke or Not Revoke? The Political Determinants of Executive Order Longevity (v1.1). Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/LZGQOH

Thrower, S. (2017). To Revoke or Not Revoke? The Political Determinants of Executive Order Longevity. American Journal of Political Science, 61. https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12294
